5 things we check in a new ad account before looking at a single campaign.

Any founder can run these in an afternoon.

1. Is tracking telling the truth?

Place one real test order and trace it through every platform. If the numbers don't match, nothing else matters yet.

2. What does the business actually need?

ROAS, new customers or profit. Agree one before touching anything. Otherwise the account chases a number nobody chose.

3. Is the structure fighting the algorithm?

Too many campaigns and ad sets split the budget so thin that nothing gets enough data to learn. Fewer, bigger ad sets learn faster.

4. How old is the creative?

If your best ad is six months old, new ones are overdue. Fresh creative is often the cheapest fix in the account.

5. Who is it really reaching?

Great ROAS can just be people who would have bought anyway. Check new vs returning customers, not just ROAS.

Which one would worry you most?

Eight months ago I went independent and started @Vizz Ads.

A few honest lessons so far:

1. Running ads is the easy part.
After 13 years, the work itself felt familiar from day one. Finding the right clients is the real job.

2. Saying no is a skill.
Some briefs weren't the right fit. Turning them down early saved everyone time.

3. Being small is an advantage.
Clients get the person who actually does the work. No handoffs, no juniors, no waiting.

4. Building in public feels uncomfortable.
Posting here still doesn't come naturally. But every conversation that's started from a post has been worth it.

5. The network you built before matters more than you think.
Thank you to everyone who's reached out, referred someone, or just cheered from the sidelines.

Still early. Still learning. Grateful for all of it.

Black Friday is four weeks away. Most brands will start planning their ads in three.

What wins Black Friday happens now, not in November. Here's what we're doing with @Vizz Ads clients this week:

→ Test your creative now
You need proven ads going in, not untested ones. Launch new concepts now so you know your winners before costs spike.

→ Build your warm audiences
Ad costs climb sharply in late November. People who've already engaged with you are far cheaper to convert. Spend now to fill those pools.

→ Fix tracking before the rush
If something breaks on the busiest weekend of the year, you're flying blind with your biggest budget.

→ Agree the offer early
Last-minute discount decisions mean last-minute creative, which means rushed ads.

→ Plan beyond the weekend
Cyber Monday and the December gifting window often beat Black Friday itself for considered purchases.

The brands that look calm on the day did the work in October.

Where are you up to?

posts.alt: Vizz Ads card: Regulated brand? You can still run good ads.
posts.linkedin_text:
Regulated doesn't have to mean boring.

At @Vizz Ads we run Meta and Google ads for an FCA-regulated investment platform. Working in a regulated category has sharpened how we brief, write and build every ad.

Three things it's taught us:

→ Compliance is a brief, not a blocker
Knowing the rules before the first idea, not after the first draft, leads to better ideas and fewer rewrites.

→ Specific beats bold
You can't promise returns. So the ads win on real detail and plain words, which tends to persuade better anyway.

→ Build the warning in, never bolt it on
The risk warning comes from an approved template on every asset. One less thing to get wrong at speed.

If you're in finance, health or any category with rules, good ads are still on the table.

What's the hardest rule you work around?

posts.linkedin_text:
Nobody hires an interior designer from an ad alone.

At @Vizz Ads we run Meta lead ads for Anyon, a premium interior design studio. For a service like this, the sale starts with a conversation, so the ads are built to start one:

→ Offer a consultation
Invite homeowners to talk to a designer about their project. The first step feels smaller and safer than a hard sell.

→ Keep the form short
A few simple questions, so the design team can follow up quickly and personally.

→ Speak to who's hiring
Homeowners, designers and decorators hire for different reasons. Speak to each one.

If your service needs a chat before a sale, your ads should start that chat.

What does the first conversation look like for your customers?

→ Winning ads
Editing a live winner resets what Meta has learned, right when you need it most.

→ Big budget jumps
Raise in small steps. A sudden doubling can knock delivery off course.

→ Untested new ideas
New ads need time to learn. Save them for December.

What we are doing: checking tracking every morning, and keeping an eye on stock and the site.

Calm accounts win the weekend. What's your one rule for Black Friday week?

posts.alt: Vizz Ads card: Who's on your own name on Google? We check, free. A sample Google Competitor Ad Check for a made-up brand.
posts.linkedin_text:
Who's sitting on your brand name on Google?

People who type your name have already chosen you. If a rival's ad sits above yours there, it's the last thing they read before they click.

The @Vizz Ads Free Competitor Ad Check now covers Google as well as Meta:

→ Every ad Google lists for you and up to three rivals, from its public Ads Transparency Center
→ Live searches on your name and your category, run three times across a day
→ A scorecard, the three biggest gaps and three tests to close them, in 48 hours

Why three times? Google shows different ads at different times. An ad not seen in one search can still be running, so we report "seen in 2 of 3 checks", never a plain yes or no.

We tested it on a real UK homeware brand (name withheld). On a search for its own brand name, rival ads were seen in 2 of 2 checks: one rival the first time, three different rivals the second. And over 30 days, its three rivals each put out 57 or more new Google ads. It put out 7.

Free, no card, no access to your ad account. Pick Meta, Google or both: vizzads.com/competitor-ad-check

posts.alt: Vizz Ads card: We read first, then we change.
posts.linkedin_text:
The most expensive thing in a new ad account is changing too much in week one.

So at @Vizz Ads every new account starts with a read, not a rebuild. We go through its whole history and sort every ad into three piles:

→ Working
Proven ideas we build on, with new versions of what already wins.

→ Tired
Ideas that worked but have been seen too often. They need a fresh take, not a new strategy.

→ Still learning
Too new to judge. Touching them now just resets the clock.

Only then do we change anything. It's built into our system, so it happens the same way on every account.

Which pile is your best ad in?

posts.alt: Vizz Ads card: Every Monday, every ad gets a verdict.
posts.linkedin_text:
"Let's give it another week" is how most ad budgets leak.

At @Vizz Ads we replaced it with a Monday checklist. Every live ad is judged against fixed pass marks, set from the account's own best results, and checked against the shop's own new customers, not just the platform's numbers.

Each ad gets one of four verdicts:

→ Keep: it passes, so we build on it
→ Refresh: the idea works, the version is tired
→ Fix: people click but don't buy, so we fix the page or the offer, not the ad
→ Stop: it fails, so the money moves to what works

Same rules, every account, every week. No gut feel.

How do you decide when to switch an ad off?

posts.alt: Vizz Ads card: AI makes the picture. We write the words.
posts.linkedin_text:
Most AI ad pictures fall down on the words: wrong font, a misspelt offer, a price that's slightly off.

So at @Vizz Ads we split the job in two.

→ AI makes the picture
Every picture starts as a checked brief, and the AI leaves space for the words but draws none of them.

→ We set the words
Headline, offer and button go on afterwards, in the brand's own fonts, the same way every time.

→ Every word gets read back
An automatic check confirms every line and every number before a person looks at it.

The result: when an offer or a legal line changes, we change the words, not the picture. It works the same for Meta ads and for Google's image and Performance Max ads.

What slows down your new ads the most?

posts.linkedin_text:
How do you know a read of someone's ads from the outside is right?

We checked ours.

Before launching the Google version of our free check, @Vizz Ads read Google's public ad data for an account we run, then compared it with the account itself:

→ For every campaign we checked, the launch and stop dates we read in public matched the account to the day: brand search, Performance Max and Demand Gen
→ Google lists Performance Max ads in public that never appear in the account's own ad report
→ One search proves nothing: a rival sat above the brand on its own name at 12:15 and was gone by 12:35. So every search now runs three times across a day
→ An ad blocker was hiding ads in our first test. Every check now runs with it off

Public data shows what's running, not what's working. But what it shows, it shows accurately.

That's what goes into every Free Competitor Ad Check, on Meta or Google: vizzads.com/competitor-ad-check
